definition.name: Create link

transport.deadline: One total request deadline includes verification, duplicate waiting, allocation attempts and commit; no phase gets an additional deadline.

authentication.verification: A pinned trusted verifier must verify authenticity, configured trusted issuer, intended audience and time validity before a stable issuer+subject principal is accepted. Raw identity headers and unverified token claims are never principals. Any authenticated principal may create; no extra scopes or claims are implied.

validation.destination: Parse an absolute URL using the WHATWG URL parser without a base; require http: or https:, a nonempty host and no username/password; serialize with the URL serializer. Reject a serialized destination above 2048 UTF-8 bytes. Do not fetch the destination; no reputation or reachability guarantee.
validation.expiry: Optional expiry; omission and null normalize to null. Otherwise require RFC3339 with an explicit offset, representable as a UTC millisecond timestamp within 0001-01-01T00:00:00.000Z..9999-12-31T23:59:59.999Z; reject excess fractional precision rather than truncate. Normalize to UTC with exactly 3 fraction digits. A new request requires expiry strictly after acceptance time.
order: Verify principal. Parse closed request, key, destination and expiry syntax/range and calculate normalized fingerprint. Invalid input/auth consumes no key.

Look up principal+exact operation ID/version+case-sensitive key. If retained success exists, equal normalized fingerprint replays the original201 status/body, even after link expiry; unequal fingerprint conflicts.

For a new or post-retention request, enforce future expiry. Exclusively serialize scoped-key attempts before allocation; concurrent requests resolve against the committed fingerprint/result or wait within the single deadline.

idempotency.key: 1..128 non-whitespace printableASCII characters (U+0021..U+007E), opaque and case-sensitive; this is not an auth credential.
idempotency.retention: Retain original successful status/body and fingerprint for 24 hours from durable commit, independently of link expiry. A key becomes eligible as a new request at commit+24h; late physical cleanup must not extend this promise. A new request is revalidated and may allocate a new code.
idempotency.concurrent: Serialize attempts exclusively for principal+operation+key before allocation. Duplicates wait within the single total 10-second request deadline. Once a prior normalized fingerprint and outcome become observable, equal retained success replays; changed payload conflicts. If an in-flight transaction or commit outcome cannot be determined by that deadline, return dependency-failure and retry the same key. Proven rollback releases the claim. No durable pending/lease state machine is implied.
idempotency.failure: Invalid/auth errors never reserve a key. Proven rolled-back attempts release the reservation; allocation-exhausted is returned only after rollback. An unknown commit outcome is dependency-failure, never a guessed success or a new allocation; retries reconcile the same key before allocation. A durable success is never replaced by a failure or another link within retention.

allocation.uniqueness: Server allocates cryptographically random codes in one public namespace and enforces a durable unique constraint. At most 5 total allocation attempts, including the initial attempt, fit within the single deadline. After 5 proven collisions, roll back and return allocation-exhausted. RNG, store or deadline failure returns dependency-failure. No custom slugs.

commit.atomicity: Link(code, immutable serialized destination, normalized expiry, verified creator principal, createdAt) and successful idempotency fingerprint/status/body commit atomically in the same authoritative durable transaction before 201. Links survive idempotency retention; never reuse an allocated code for another destination.
commit.success: Replay original status/body, not a newly generated code, timestamp or origin URL. Future resolve policy must read the authoritative committed record; this create declaration does not supply resolve/cache policy.

behavior.limits: Declarative operation intent only; this record defines no handler, adapter, generator or runtime implementation.

sourceReview.meaning: Sources inform this finite behavior; they do not define the application-specific idempotency or allocation choices.
sourceReview.postgresqlMeaning: Sources explain why uncommitted fingerprints need bounded serialization; this contract selects no database adapter or PostgreSQL version.

definition.requestEnvelope: The request schema describes the normalized operation-owned Idempotency-Key header and JSON body after HTTP header-name normalization and the trusted authentication boundary. Other transport/auth headers are outside this closed envelope; it is not the entire raw HTTP request.
